[NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) uses residual causal dilated convolutions to expand temporal receptive fields without pooling. This makes block-by-position activation patching a plausible diagnostic, although the retrieved literature does not establish a validated NextItNet-specific protocol. [Zhang and Nanda, ICLR 2024](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=Hf17y6u9BC), show that corruption methods and evaluation metrics can substantially change localization results; their evidence concerns language models, so transfer to recommendation requires validation.

[Heimersheim and Nanda, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255), distinguish clean-to-corrupted patching, which tests restoration, from corrupted-to-clean patching, which tests disruption. Proposed adaptation: cache matched histories and patch individual convolutional blocks at selected recent positions, recomputing downstream layers. Measure raw target-versus-fixed-negative score margins alongside validation HR@10; report normalized recovery only when the clean–corrupted gap is substantial. Restoration alone does not establish necessity or a unique information-storage location.

Recommended controls, rather than established NextItNet findings: identical-history patches should reproduce original scores; padding interventions and changes outside the readout’s receptive field should have negligible effects. Compare recent swaps, older-history permutations, and frequency-matched replacements while preserving left padding, history length, and final nonpadding readout. Stratify effects by item frequency and history length. Validate patching machinery with deterministic synthetic dependencies without fitting extra models. A [2026 RecSys study](https://research.atspotify.com/publications/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-really-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) reports strong recency-weighted pairwise probes on several benchmarks, reinforcing that order sensitivity alone does not demonstrate higher-order reasoning. All interventions can examine the existing single trained NextItNet per category.
